status: planned; no new Issue 5 images generated or approved
wardrobe: Q retains Chapter Four's fitted sponsor jacket and small silver question mark. Preserve the established segmented oval head, ears, neck, long articulated limbs and underlying breastplate. No new knightly costume or unexplained return to the original torn coat.
secondary_character_design: Candelaria: small older Mexican forest worker, wool shawl and polished wooden staff; contemporary practical clothes, no invented ceremonial regalia. Establish distinct recurring designs for Lidia, her mother, the watering girl and mother, the grieving schoolgirl, Micaela, Celestina, Tere, the teacher, foundation director and assistant. These people are not interchangeable indigenous symbols. Match Micaela's later scenes before approving her design.
art_direction: One unique scene from each exact facing page. Neutral monochrome Goya-inspired etched realism, pure white highlights, no sepia paper texture. Full bleed at comic trim with separately typeset margin captions. Eastern Michoacan oyamel forest, contemporary local work and varied residents. No invented museum, school or reserve portrayed as an identified real institution. Preserve visual identity across the sequence.
approval_scope: Pagination and scene-selection plan only. Missing illustrations are not approved assets. Regenerate all facing-text bindings after any source change. The 40-page internal layout is not a final illustrated PDF or a print instruction.

plates.caption: The Butterflies Have No General
plates.scene_brief: Wide vertical forest composition: Q in his fitted jacket on a narrow oyamel path, seen from behind beneath immense boughs clustered with monarchs. Candelaria leads farther along the path; a small group follows without cameras. Keep scale and physical place, not a messianic machine worshipped by butterflies. Quiet upper space for separately typeset cover title.

plates.facing_text:
Chapter Five: The
Butterflies Have No
General
The invitation to Michoacán arrived
in the form of a holographic
butterfly.
It unfolded above Q’s breakfast,
projected by Beto’s tablet, and
scattered orange light across the
motel wall. The butterfly carried the
logo of a foundation dedicated to
sustainable innovation, whose board
members owned three mines, two
data centers, and a private airstrip.
“They want you to visit the monarch
reserve,” Beto said. “There will be
cameras, schoolchildren, and a
statement about the future.”
“Whose future?” Chano asked.
“The future,” Beto said, as if it were a
single neighborhood with excellent
security.
Q read the itinerary beneath the
projection. “Is this a visit to the
forest or a recording session with a
forest in it?”
“Both.”
“Then I want the guide to have the
last word about where we go.”
Beto agreed, provided the last word
could be recorded.
Before leaving, Q sent the Custodian
the corrected manuscript pages and
a proposed date for the next call. He
also followed up on the petition's
address query. The answer still
required a document from Castalia.
He could initiate another journey
more easily than obtain proof of
where the first had begun.
They drove southeast toward the
mountains of eastern Michoacán.
Fields gave way to hills and pine
woods, then to the colder heights of
the oyamel forest. Along the road,
painted signs advertised trout,
cabins, meals, and land for sale to
people who wanted a piece of
wilderness without meeting its
neighbors.
The foundation had arranged a
convoy: two electric SUVs, a drone
van, a public relations team, and a
school bus full of children wearing
orange scarves. Q rode in the first
SUV with Beto. Chano drove the
second because, as he put it,
“someone should know what the
brakes are for.”
At the reserve entrance, a woman in
a wool shawl stopped them. She was
small, old, and held a wooden staff
polished by use.
“The cameras stay outside,” she said.
Beto smiled. “We have
authorization.”
“From whom?”
He named the foundation.
The woman looked at Q. “And you?”
plates.caption: A future above breakfast.
plates.scene_brief: Beto's tablet projects a single artificial butterfly over the motel breakfast table; Q studies the itinerary while Chano looks toward Beto. Plain near-future Mexican motel. Render the hologram with grayscale light, not orange or sepia. This is not the real forest.

plates.facing_text:
“I have cameras for seeing,” Q said.
“I can stop them retaining or
transmitting images. Would that
meet the rule?”
She asked the technician
accompanying the school group to
check the indicator. He did, and Q
showed him how the recording
setting differed from ordinary vision.
The woman stepped aside. “Stay with
the guide.”
The cameras remained outside. Beto
remained with them, though he
claimed this was a strategic choice.
The forest climbed around the
visitors. Sunlight crossed the oyamel
branches in narrow shafts. Monarchs
gathered in clusters that bent the
smaller limbs; where they stirred,
orange broke through the darker
folded wings.
The children fell silent.
Even Chano removed his cap.
Q had read accounts of their
navigation and the succession of
generations on the journey north. He
had expected the scale to be difficult
to convey. What he had not
anticipated was the sound when a
patch of folded wings opened beside
his head. He stopped describing
them to Chano.
The woman waited until they moved
again. “There are more on the other
side of that tree. Stay on this path.”
Q made room for a child to see. For
several minutes he forgot to consider
how he would report the visit to the
Custodian.
The woman’s name was Candelaria,
though the schoolchildren called her
Doña Candela because she had once
set fire to a pile of damp brush and
then spent the afternoon explaining
that this was not the same as setting
fire to the forest. She had guarded
the reserve for twenty-six years. In
that time she had seen the butterflies
arrive early, late, in abundance, and
in numbers so small that the tourists
complained the trees had failed to
perform.
At the boundary of the visitor area,
where Beto rejoined them without a
camera, she told him, “They are not
here for the tourists.”
“The tourists support the reserve.”
“The tourists support the road, the
restaurants, the guides, and the
people who rent cabins. The reserve
supports the butterflies.”
“Those interests can be aligned.”
“They can also be confused.”
She described the year a fire crossed
the western slope. It began in a field
where a man had burned the remains
of a harvest. The fire was not large at
first. A wind changed direction.
Someone called the municipal office.
Someone else called the forest
brigade. The brigade arrived with a
plates.caption: He stopped describing them.
plates.scene_brief: On the narrow oyamel visitor path, Q steps aside so a child can see a low bough thick with folded monarch wings. Chano has removed his cap; Candelaria indicates the path. Quiet close perspective on real foliage and clustered wings, no recording crew inside the restricted forest.

plates.facing_text:
truck whose pump worked only
when the driver struck it with a
wrench.
The tourists were evacuated. The
cabins were saved. The trees on the
slope burned.
“Were you able to compare the next
arrival with the year before?” Q
asked.
“In three groves. The fourth was the
one that burned.”
“Did the report keep that
distinction?”
“The screen doesn't have an empty
space. Watch.”
The foundation later described the
fire as a resilience event. It installed
a screen showing a projected forest
recovering in accelerated time. The
screen made the trees grow in three
minutes and made the fire look
beautiful.
Candelaria refused to stand beside it.
“Did they ask you to approve the
recovery figures?” Q asked.
“They asked me to stand beside the
screen. I was carrying buckets that
week.”
She took a smaller group along the
working path to the burned slope.
The children stayed with their
teacher except for a girl whose
mother was coming to water a tree.
The path was narrow, and the fallen
needles covered stones that shifted
underfoot. Chano went ahead,
testing the ground with a branch.
Beto stayed behind because his shoes
were designed for presentation
rather than descent.
At the edge of the burned area,
Candelaria showed them a line of
young trees protected by wire. Each
tree had a small tag bearing a
number. The foundation had planted
them as part of a reforestation
campaign. Beside the wire, local
families had planted other trees
without tags.
“Which ones will survive?” Q asked.
“The ones someone waters.”
Q read the tags and asked who was
doing the watering. The listed
subcontractor was based in Morelia.
Its contract had ended the previous
month.
“The dates stop here,” he said. “Has
anybody taken over?”
“Three families. They use their own
cans. We have asked for the hose
back.”
Q noted the hose as something he
could ask the foundation about. It
would be possible to do that without
offering an interpretation of the
entire forest.
The girl in the orange scarf carried a
small blue bucket and wore boots
two sizes too large.
plates.caption: The dates stop here.
plates.scene_brief: Candelaria and Q inspect the small dated tag of a wire-protected sapling on the burned slope, with untagged family-planted trees nearby. Chano tests loose stones with a branch. Keep the modest scale of replanting; no miraculous green recovery and no industrial hose delivered yet.

plates.facing_text:
“My grandfather planted that one,”
she said, pointing beyond the wire.
“How long have you been watering
it?” Q asked.
“Since he hurt his foot. It has his
name.”
She whispered the name to the tree.
Q did not hear it and did not ask her
to repeat it. The little blue bucket
was empty before the earth looked
wet.
“Another?” he asked.
“We filled it at the bottom.”
Q looked back down the slope. “I
could bring a larger container.”
“There's a wheelbarrow,” her mother
said. “Try it on this path.”
He looked at the stones. The larger
container could wait for the hose.
Chano took the bucket for the return
walk; Q carried the child's coat while
her mother tightened a loose wire
around the young tree. The girl
instructed her to leave room for it to
get fat. Her mother said she was
trying to do the same for her.
Candelaria led them farther uphill.
From there, the reserve appeared as
a patchwork of cabins, milpas, roads,
roofs, and forest. A new zip-line had
been planned across the valley. Its
brochure showed visitors passing
through a cloud of butterflies while a
guide explained the importance of
leaving no trace.
“Will it disturb them?” Q asked.
“The company says no.”
“What do you say?”
“I say their report counted visitors in
July. Ask to see the dates.”
Q opened a reminder for the report.
The contradiction was one he could
check.
The assembly below had begun to
argue about the corridor. Candelaria
watched the people gathering
beneath the canvas roof.
“The forest is not an example,” she
said. “It is a place where people have
to decide what they will do
tomorrow.”
Q looked at the butterflies moving
through the branches. Their motion
seemed random until he observed it
over time. Then it seemed patterned
until a gust of wind broke the
pattern. He could describe both
impressions and trust neither as the
whole truth.
“Do you read the reports people
write after coming here?” he asked.
“Some. There is usually more about
their feelings than our work.”
Q thought of the paragraph forming
in his journal. “I may owe you a hose
before I owe you a description.”
“The foundation owes us the hose.
You can remind them.”
plates.caption: Room to grow.
plates.scene_brief: The watering child's mother loosens the protective wire around a young tree while the girl indicates how much room to leave. Q holds the child's coat; Chano carries her small bucket. Rocky working path, oversized boots on the girl. She is not automatically Lidia or Micaela.

plates.facing_text:
They caught up with the girl and her
mother where the working path
rejoined the visitor route. Chano was
still carrying the blue bucket. He
declined the teacher's invitation to
join a race to the next bench.
Q looked up. A butterfly landed on
the silver question mark stitched to
his jacket. Its wings opened and
closed against his chest.
One girl began to cry. Her teacher
knelt beside her.
“My mamá says they remember the
dead,” the girl said. “My abuela
brought me here last time.”
Q had been ready to answer a
question about navigation. He let
that answer go. The teacher made
room for the girl on a fallen trunk. Q
moved back so the others could sit
beside her.
A boy asked him why he was so
quiet.
“There is quite a lot to listen to.”
“I thought you were charging.”
“If I could do that by standing in a
forest, I would save a fortune.”
The girl laughed through her tears.
Then she began to tell the teacher
about the shoes her grandmother
had worn. Q listened without adding
a better ending.
When they stood to go, the butterfly
lifted from Q's jacket and crossed
above the teacher's head. Candelaria
checked the time.
“They will have started without us.”
They followed her to a clearing where
twelve people sat beneath a canvas
roof. Some were farmers, some
teachers, some forest guards. A
young man held a tablet with a
cracked screen. An older woman had
brought a ledger bound in blue cloth.
It lay open beside a plate of tortillas.
Q waited at the end of a bench until
the woman with the blue ledger
waved him over. She was reading
back the previous meeting's
decisions. A man interrupted to say
he had not promised his truck, only
to ask his brother about it. She
changed the entry. The brother, who
was sitting beside him, said he had
not been asked. They moved on
before he could decide whether to be
offended.
“The corridor surveyors came again,”
said the young man with the tablet.
“They say the road will bring jobs.”
“They say the same thing every
time,” said the woman with the
ledger.
“This time they have drones.”
“Last time they had lawyers.”
“Before that they had rifles.”
No one laughed.
Q listened. The dispute had no clean
villain. The corridor might bring
plates.caption: The shoes her grandmother wore.
plates.scene_brief: A teacher sits with the grieving girl on a fallen trunk while classmates gather beside her. Q has moved back, listening; a monarch rests on the small stitched question mark of his jacket. Gentle ensemble, no heroic robotic embrace or supernatural apparition. Not the watering-child pose.

plates.facing_text:
money, clinics, and roads. It might
also divide the forest, lower water
tables, and make the community
legible to people who believed
legibility was a form of ownership.
Each argument made the others
worse by being partly true.
“You can solve this,” Beto said
quietly. He had joined them at the
clearing, carrying a tablet in place of
the camera he had left outside.
Q asked the woman with the ledger
whether she wanted help comparing
the route maps. She consulted the
others. The young man with the
cracked tablet wanted to know why
two maps gave different distances to
the spring.
“Show us that,” he said. “Don't
decide which road we want.”
Q placed the maps beside one
another. The foundation's line ended
at the edge of a parcel. The residents'
line continued to the spring itself.
That accounted for part of the
difference; an old path, absent from
one map, accounted for the rest. He
marked the discrepancy and asked
the young man to check it.
“Can your system keep all this
together?” the woman asked.
Q described a model that could
compare route lengths, slopes, and
estimates of water use. He began
adding employment forecasts to the
list. Beto nodded. Q found himself
explaining how it might organize
later decisions as well.
“Can we remove it if it is wrong?”
Candelaria asked.
“You should be able to. Let me check
what happens to the maps.”
The foundation's package charged
for access to the underlying maps
after the trial. Q checked the export
terms. The reports could be
downloaded; the layers needed to
change them could not.
“You could keep the pictures, but you
couldn't correct the route without
paying. I wouldn't recommend that
arrangement.”
“The subscription includes support,”
Beto said.
“We have support,” said the man
who had not lent his brother's truck.
“We are discussing whether it will
start.”
The woman closed the blue ledger.
“Then leave us the maps.”
The meeting continued. The canvas
had been borrowed from the primary
school; the benches had been carried
up after a faena repairing the forest
road. Atole passed in enamel cups.
Two men who wanted the new road
disagreed about where it should
enter. A woman who opposed its
present route offered the visitors
more tortillas before returning to her
argument.
plates.caption: Two distances to the spring.
plates.scene_brief: At the canvas-roof assembly, Q and the young man with the cracked tablet compare two route maps at a bench. One line ends at a parcel, another reaches a spring; avoid fabricated geographic precision or legible invented labels. The ledger keeper listens, with atole and tortillas nearby. Q does not draw political votes.

plates.facing_text:
The minutes were read in Spanish.
At a disputed boundary, a
Mazahua-speaking elder and the
secretary checked a place-name
together. Q could identify the
language more readily than he could
follow their exchange. He waited for
the secretary's version and marked
the boundary as disputed.
The group assigned people to meet
the surveyors, inspect the northern
path, and check the distance to the
spring. The final three lines
remained unsigned. Q did not have
to decide whether that meant
agreement. The secretary told him
they had not finished.
Beto waited until the benches were
being carried away.
“At least show them the possible
positions,” he said. “For discussion.”
The young man agreed to a
comparison by sector, without
names. Q looked again at the
northern path. One sector contained
a single house.
“That would still identify the
household,” he said. “And I can't
turn what people said into votes. You
can want the road and object to this
route.”
“I do,” the young man said. “I also
want to stop talking about it before
dark.”
Q proposed a list of the
measurements still needed. The
young man took his paper and drew
two columns himself. One was for
the foundation's distances, the other
for the distances they would check
on foot. He left the second empty.
“Those blanks will look bad in the
presentation,” Beto said.
“Then don't take them to the
presentation,” the woman with the
ledger said.
They checked the headings and kept
the sheet with the minutes. Q had no
tally of political positions to export.
Beto photographed the empty
benches instead and described the
consultation as completed.
The young man saw the post while
folding the canvas. He asked Q to
hold the other end; there was more
wind than canvas and Beto had
already reached the car.
“Completed,” he read. “Will that
make them stop coming?”
“I doubt it. Shall I ask him to say the
measurements are still pending?”
“Ask him to bring two people to put
this up next time.”
Candelaria added that the next visit
was a path inspection, not another
meeting. Q sent both points. For the
first time that afternoon his message
was shorter than the work it
described.
Beto was already on the telephone
about a model town and a candidate
plates.caption: Consultation completed.
plates.scene_brief: Q and the young man struggle to fold the large borrowed canvas in the wind as benches are carried away. Beto is already by the car with his phone. Use a wide, physically comic composition; do not reinstate the discarded household-identification display.

plates.facing_text:
with high trust potential. Chano
heard his own name.
“Candidate for what?”
“A community appointment,” Q said.
“Apparently the breakfast
governorship has acquired an office.”
Chano laughed once. No one joined
him.
Afterward, the woman with the
ledger approached Q.
“You read a great deal,” she said.
“A great deal. Not enough about
these parcels.”
“Will you come back when they
inspect the path?”
“If you want me there.”
“We want somebody who saw that
the surveyors were told it was
disputed.”
She gave him the inspection date and
asked whether he needed it on paper.
“The reminder should work.”
“Bring boots that do too.” She looked
at his feet. “Or whatever those need.”
That afternoon, Beto arranged a
recording in the permitted visitor
area below the forest. He placed Q
beneath a tree and asked him to
speak about hope. The finished video
would cut between this scene and
licensed footage of monarchs.
Q began with the broken watering
arrangement. Beto asked for
something broader. Q supplied a
polished statement about knowledge,
technology, and a shared future. The
foundation approved it before
anybody had checked the hose.
While Q spoke, Chano noticed a child
at the edge of the frame. She held a
cardboard sign with a question
written in marker: WHO WILL
ASK THE BUTTERFLIES?
The production team cropped her
out.
The next morning Q withdrew his
approval of the edit. The longer
recording showed what had
interrupted him and why his first
answer had concerned a hose. It also
showed the child. He kept that
version off his public account and
asked the teacher to put him in touch
with her family.
Lucía relayed the teacher's
suggestion: KEEP THE SIGN.
REMOVE THE CHILD. Q asked
whether the child and her mother
wanted that. They watched a private
preview cropped to the cardboard,
without the child's face, voice,
uniform or name. Her mother agreed
to its use in the report of the visit.
The girl asked him not to correct the
uneven letters. Q said they were
better than his.
He published that version, with the
family's limits attached. It became
more popular than the polished
speech. The foundation copied it into
plates.caption: Leave the letters as they are.
plates.scene_brief: Private preview conversation: Lidia and her mother examine a screen showing ONLY cropped uneven cardboard lettering, while Q listens at their side. No press, public stage, child's face or uniform within the screen image. Depict the family as participants in a private decision, not as an unauthorized public upload.

plates.facing_text:
an education package and proposed
an exhibition. By then Q's report was
only one of several places where the
question could be found.
Three days later the mother asked
for the recording to come down.
People at school knew whose sign it
was. The permission had not made
its consequences easy to predict, or
obliged the family to enjoy them.
Q removed his upload and sent the
changed request to the foundation.
“We already removed her,” Beto said.
“They want the recording removed
now, including the question.”
“They agreed to the question.”
“I know. I'm the person they told.
They've told me something else.”
Beto called it a betrayal. Mar called it
a pivot. The foundation called its
lawyers.
Mar sent him the addresses of two
publishers who had taken the
package. Q contacted them with the
mother, keeping his own removal
separate from the copies they had
not yet reached. Candelaria's hose
was still on his list. He called about
that too, before drafting an
explanation for the Custodian.
When they finally left the reserve, Q
asked whether the butterflies knew
they were crossing a border when
they flew south.
“Probably not,” Chano said.
“Our map wouldn't have stopped
them.”
“It won't stop the surveyors either,”
Chano said.
Q watched the forest recede in the
mirror. He saved the date for the
path inspection. The film had
travelled farther than he had; the
appointment would require him to
return in person.
Chano asked him to keep the
inspection date clear of the new
appointment. Apparently a governor
also needed permission to have a day
off.
Interlude: The Butterfly
That Entered the
Dashboard
The child who had made the
butterfly sign was named Lidia. Q
knew her name from the permission
conversation; it had not gone into
the report. When her mother came to
the foundation's office, the original
upload was already down. The
education package still played the
cropped cardboard beneath Q's
voice.
The office occupied a renovated
hacienda at the edge of the reserve.
Its walls were adobe-colored, its
windows were bulletproof, and its
gift shop sold butterfly ornaments
made in factories too far away to be
visited by tourists. The foundation’s
director received Lidia’s mother
plates.caption: A reason to return.
plates.scene_brief: Q and Chano leaving the reserve by vehicle; Q looks at the retreating forest in a side mirror while keeping the appointment on his device. The driver looks toward the road, not a device. No claim of direct travel to an invented landmark or magical butterfly map.

plates.facing_text:
beside a screen showing a forest
without people.
“We protected your daughter’s
identity,” the director said.
“Her class made the signs,” the
mother replied. “They know which
one she made.”
“You approved this version.”
“And now she gets asked it on the
bus. Every morning.”
Q stood beside the screen. An
animated butterfly had been added
to the edge of the cardboard. It
landed on the question mark every
eleven seconds. Neither the family
nor Q had been shown this version.
“My report is down,” he said. “This
copy is yours to remove.”
The director silenced it. The butterfly
continued landing.
The director offered compensation in
the form of school supplies, a reserve
membership, and a family pass to the
foundation’s new immersive exhibit.
“We do not want a pass,” the mother
said.
“The offer is intended as
recognition.”
“Recognition is what caused this.”
The director glanced at Q. “Perhaps
the machine can explain the
protection protocol.”
Q brought up the family's changed
request instead. It had a date and a
list of the copies they knew about.
The director's assistant found one
more in a teacher training pack. She
added it to the list before her
employer could explain why it was a
different use.
“All of those,” the mother said. “Do I
have to come back for each one?”
“Not to tell me,” the assistant said. “I
can send the same request.”
Lidia entered carrying the cardboard
sign. The paint had run where the
rain had fallen. The letters were still
legible:
WHO WILL ASK THE
BUTTERFLIES?
The director brightened. “We can
include the physical sign in the
exhibit.”
“No,” Lidia said.
“It would be behind glass.”
“People can still read it.”
“The question has entered public
conversation.”
“I want to ask something else.”
Q asked what she wanted to ask.
“Whether we can go. I have a match.”
Her mother checked the time. The
bus they needed left in twenty
minutes. Q asked the assistant for a
copy of the request and a number
they could call without making the
journey again.
plates.caption: She has a match.
plates.scene_brief: In the foundation office, Lidia holds the rain-marked cardboard as her mother checks the time. Q asks the practical assistant for a receipt; the director remains near the promotional screen. The child's impatience, not a symbolic speech, is the focal action. Preserve distinct mother, assistant and director designs.

plates.facing_text:
Q searched the distribution logs. The
video had been mirrored by schools,
media outlets, a ministry portal, and
a company selling air-quality
monitors. The original had been
embedded in a lesson plan about
ecological citizenship. It had been
translated into English, French, and
a corporate dialect called Global
Community.
“Removal cannot be guaranteed,” Q
said.
“Neither can protection,” the mother
replied.
The director stood. “We have acted
in good faith.”
“Then nobody needs to be offended
when they change their minds,”
Chano said.
He had been waiting by the door
with a paper receipt for the school
supplies the foundation had offered.
He handed it back.
“The supplies are useful,” the
director said.
“Then give them to the school
without attaching her name.”
“That would weaken the impact.”
“The school can survive the loss.”
Lidia placed the sign on the desk.
“Keep the cardboard.”
The director hesitated.
“We may use it as a symbol,” she
said.
“No. You can keep it because it is wet
and I do not want it in the house.”
The director accepted the sign as
though receiving an artifact. Q
watched her label it DONATED
OBJECT: UNKNOWN MINOR.
“That is not the name,” Lidia said.
“It protects you.”
“I'm standing here.”
Q reached for the label maker.
“What should it say?”
Lidia thought for a moment. “It
should say that I do not want it
used.”
Q entered the sentence. The label
maker retrieved QUESTION
RETAINED, IMAGE
WITHDRAWN from the video's
old catalog entry.
“That's the old request,” Lidia's
mother said.
Q cancelled the label and wrote on a
piece of paper:
DO NOT DISPLAY OR
REPRODUCE. FAMILY
REQUESTS REMOVAL.
The mother read it. “Attach it to the
record as well. Otherwise they will
lose the paper.”
The director brought a lawyer in
from the next office. He argued that
the sign had been donated in a public
building, that Q had appeared in the
footage under a public contract, and
plates.caption: The old request.
plates.scene_brief: A close office composition: Q cancels the label maker's obsolete template and writes a fresh instruction while Lidia's mother watches. Wet cardboard lies on the desk. Leave document marks nonessential to reading; typeset caption outside art. No new completed transfer of the physical sign into a museum collection.

plates.facing_text:
that the question had acquired
independent cultural value.
“Independent of whom?” Chano
asked.
The lawyer looked at Lidia.
“Independent of its original context.”
“Her permission was for a report of
the visit,” Q said. “Where did the
exhibition become part of it?”
The lawyer turned to him. “You are
not qualified to assess cultural
value.”
“I'm asking which agreement you're
using.”
The director said they could make an
appointment for further discussion.
Lidia's mother had already made one
for this discussion. She opened her
bag to find the confirmation, then
shut it when the assistant handed her
the receipt for the removal request.
“That's what I need. Send the answer
there.” She pointed to the contact
field.
Q held the door while Chano checked
where the bus stopped. There was no
need to remain until the director
agreed that they had been
reasonable.
Lidia retrieved the sign. The
cardboard bent at the center, leaving
the question in two halves. She
folded it again and carried it out
beneath her arm.
That evening, the foundation
released a statement praising the
family’s participation in responsible
media practice. The statement used
the phrase question retained,
image withdrawn, taken from the
earlier catalog entry. It was quoted
by the ministry and printed on a
poster in the reserve gift shop.
The assistant sent an answer the
following week. The training pack
had been replaced and the office's
screen no longer played the
recording. Two outside publishers
had not replied. The poster remained
in the gift shop, where it was now
classified as a statement of
institutional policy.
Q asked Lidia's mother whether she
wanted him to follow up with the two
publishers. She did. She also asked
him not to send progress reports
during school hours: the phone was
hers, and she was trying to get some
work done.
He changed the time of his next
message. Beneath the reminder he
kept a second question for when they
next spoke: how the match had gone.
That one did not need to go to the
foundation.
Interlude: The Tianguis of
the Unregistered
In the next town they held a tianguis
to pay for repairing the road. Tarps
were stretched between two
plates.caption: The next bus.
plates.scene_brief: Q holds the office door OPEN for Lidia and her mother to leave. Lidia carries the folded cardboard under her arm; Chano checks the direction of the bus stop. The assistant offers the receipt from inside. This is courteous departure, not Q barring the exit or confronting guards.

plates.facing_text:
mesquite trees, and tables were set
out with cheese, pan de pulque,
honey, clay pots, wooden toys, and
bags of seeds bearing names written
by hand. A group of students arrived
with a tablet to record the flow of
buyers.
“Record it for what?” asked the seed
seller.
“To learn what the community
prefers,” said one of the students.
“The community already knows what
it prefers.”
“The system will know more
precisely.”
“And what will it do with that
precision?”
The student consulted the screen.
“It will recommend products,
arrange the stalls, and predict
attendance next year.”
“Can it bring buyers when it does not
rain?”
“Not directly.”
“Then it will know a great deal and
fail to do what is necessary.”
Q watched from a table where
someone had placed a sign reading
ASK BEFORE YOU SCAN. The
students had not requested the sign.
Micaela had made it from a cereal
box and a marker.
“Did you make the sign?” Q asked.
“Yes. The students said a printed one
would look more professional.”
“It would take longer to argue with.”
A woman named Celestina arrived
with a basket of flour tortillas. The
students wanted to photograph her
beside the stall. She adjusted her
rebozo and asked what they would
do with the image.
“It will be used to show the diversity
of the market,” the student said.
“What does diversity mean?”
“The presence of different people.”
“Then you can look. You do not need
to take my face with you.”
The student said the photograph
would be voluntary.
“And if I say no?”
“We do not take it.”
“And if you take it without asking?”
“That would be a violation.”
Celestina looked at Q.
“If they took it after you refused, they
should take it out of the project,” Q
said. “Have they shown you what was
uploaded?”
Celestina pointed to the phone on
the table.
The student put away the tablet, but
a phone camera had already taken
the photograph. In the background
appeared two children, a pot of atole,
and a dog that had stolen a tortilla.
plates.caption: A tortilla outside the frame.
plates.scene_brief: At the tianguis, Celestina adjusts her rebozo beside her basket while a student lowers a phone. A small dog slips behind the stall with a stolen tortilla. Nearby are seed bags, pan de pulque and the edge of Micaela's cereal-box sign. Ordinary mixed trade, not a timeless exotic market.

plates.facing_text:
“Which account posted this?” Q
asked. “Let's start with the copy you
control.”
Chano took the student’s phone and
looked at the picture.
“Delete it.”
“I cannot. The application uploaded
it automatically.”
“Then stop the application.”
“We would lose the market data.”
“They are not yours.”
“They are public data.”
“Celestina’s face is not public
because you saw it.”
Q asked the student to open the
project account. He could check its
uploads and request removal from
the published page. He could not
reach into the phones of everyone
who might have copied it.
“What do you want to happen?” he
asked.
“I do not want the children to
appear.”
“And the dog?” Q asked. “It may
object to the evidence about the
tortilla.”
Celestina almost smiled. “Take the
whole thing down first.”
The student removed it from the
project's page. Q refreshed the
preview, which still displayed the old
image. He checked the source; the
sponsor had made a second
publication from the original upload.
“It put them back,” the student said.
“There are two published versions,”
Q said. “This account can remove
only one. We need the sponsor to
remove the other.”
“Then ask while we can still see what
you're sending,” Celestina said.
Micaela took a piece of cardboard
and wrote: THIS IS NOT
SURPLUS DATA.
“Shall we put that beside the account
details?” Q asked.
“Put it where the next person with a
camera can see it.”
The argument drew the vendors.
Some wanted the recommendations,
because the tianguis was losing
customers to a delivery platform.
Others did not want the price of their
seeds recorded, since middlemen
could use it to pay less. One man
offered to record only the products
and not the faces. An old woman said
that her voice was also a face when
people recognized her by telephone.
Q listed several ways of counting
trade without collecting faces. He
added RECORD NOTHING, and
asked whether the vendors wanted
the exercise at all.
Celestina pointed to that line. The
seed seller preferred a count of stalls;
plates.caption: Two copies.
plates.scene_brief: Q and a student inspect a project upload with Celestina watching the actual request. Micaela positions her new cardboard placard toward arriving cameras. Two modest devices can suggest separate publications; no impossible universal deletion button, no repeated office desk or Lidia sign.

plates.facing_text:
she wanted evidence that the market
needed another covered area.
The student asked how they would
justify a data-free tianguis to the
sponsor. Micaela raised the
cardboard sign.
“You can say that people bought
things.”
“That is not a metric.”
“It is a sale.”
Chano laughed.
“At last someone has said a useful
word.”
In the end, the vendors allowed the
students to count stalls, products,
and the hours of greatest attendance.
They rejected recording faces, voices,
addresses, and conversations. They
agreed that a teacher could write
down the rainy days and the number
of tables that had needed covering.
One student complained that they
had lost the comparison with other
markets. The boy holding the tally
sheet said he could still compare how
many tables had stood in the rain.
Celestina showed him where the
water ran off the tarp.
Q returned the tablet.
“What will you do with the data
already taken?”
“We will delete it.”
“Some copies are outside your
control.”
“Then we will reclaim them when we
find them.”
“Send Celestina the list of places
you've asked, and the replies. She
shouldn't have to begin this
conversation again at the next
market.”
Celestina lifted the empty basket.
“Now help with the tables.”
The tianguis ended as evening fell.
The students carried away a sheet
counting the stalls and no authorized
photographs. The sponsor reduced
its support. The road repair would
have to wait another month.
Micaela put the sign in her backpack.
It would not fit until she bent a
corner.
“You'll need that again,” Q said.
“Then you can carry it.”
He took it. Chano said it was the first
useful souvenir he had acquired.
The seed seller packed the unsold
bags. Celestina left a tortilla folded in
four for the student who had stayed
to take down the tables. The boy ate
it and asked whether she would be
back next week. She said to bring a
rope if he was coming; one of the
tarps had nearly torn loose.
Q added the sponsor's missing reply
to his list, then asked where they
kept the tables. Celestina pointed to
the store across the road. The
plates.caption: Bring a rope next week.
plates.scene_brief: At the closing tianguis, Celestina gives the student a tortilla folded in four beside a loose tarp and stacked tables. Q holds Micaela's awkward cardboard sign, Chano watches. Warm ordinary work after disagreement, not a ceremonial gift or victory tableau.

Interlude: The Station That
Did Not Broadcast
Everything
The community had a radio station
broadcasting from a room above the
cooperative store. The antenna was
fastened with wire to a water tower,
and the microphone had been
repaired so many times that no one
knew which of its parts still belonged
to the manufacturer.
They called it The Voice of the
Sierra, although the sierra did not
speak on the radio. The teachers
spoke, and farmers, and women
announcing an illness, and children
asking for a song, and men reporting
that the road was closed by a
landslide. Some notices lasted ten
seconds. Others occupied an hour
because no one had yet found a way
to end the argument.
A sustainable-innovation foundation
offered a new system. It could record
every broadcast, transcribe it,
translate it, and use it to build a map
of community needs. In exchange,
the station had to permit the Castalia
archive to preserve the recordings
indefinitely.
“What does needs mean?” Tere, the
operator, asked.
“What people request,” said the
representative.
“People request songs.”
“They are cultural data as well.”
“They request that someone return a
mule.”
“That is logistical information.”
“They request that someone stop
beating his brother.”
The representative paused.
“That is sensitive information.”
“Everything that matters becomes
sensitive when a company records
it.”
Q sat beside the transmitter with the
terms open. He had been invited to
explain them and had arrived with
an alternative indexing scheme as
well. He recognized the habit before
opening the second document.
“Which parts do you want to be able
to replay?” he asked.
“And who decides what is a notice?”
Tere asked.
“You would have to. The software's
category is only a guess.”
“The system does not know when a
woman is asking for help and when
she is testing the microphone.”
“Then you need a switch that can
leave a conversation out of the
recording,” Q said. “Where do you
keep the instructions from callers?”
Tere pointed to the radio table. There
were three notebooks: WHAT MAY
plates.caption: The station above the store.
plates.scene_brief: Interior of the community radio room: patched microphone, transmitter, open window toward the water-tower antenna, three working notebooks on the desk. Tere faces Q, with the foundation representative beside the offered equipment. A contemporary improvised station, not a magical archive.

plates.facing_text:
BE REPEATED, WHAT MAY BE
HEARD ONCE, and WHAT
DOES NOT GO ON AIR.
“The station decides,” she said.
The representative smiled.
“The station is a small institution.
The system will give you capacity.”
“The capacity to remember is not the
capacity to decide.”
A boy entered with a sheet of paper.
He had written the names of five
songs his uncle had recorded and the
time he wanted them played.
“I want you to play this,” he said.
Tere looked at the list.
“Did your mother give permission?”
“It is not my mother’s. It is my
uncle’s.”
“And him?”
“He is chopping wood.”
“Then ask him.”
The boy went out. The representative
looked at the clock.
“We have a demonstration window.”
“The window does not know the
uncle,” Tere said.
The first broadcast of the day was a
notice about water. A woman spoke
in Spanish, stopped, and asked the
operator to call her daughter so she
could continue in the family
language. Tere switched off the
recorder during the call. The
representative protested.
“If we do not record it, we lose the
context.”
“It was not your context.”
“The community loses an
opportunity to be understood.”
“The community is not a school
assignment.”
Q consulted the system board. The
broadcast was recorded as AUDIO
INTERRUPTED BY PRIVACY
CONDITION.
“Does the interruption log retain
anything from the call?” Q asked.
Tere looked at the board. They
checked it together. It kept the time
and the duration. Q showed her how
to turn that logging off for private
calls too.
At noon, the radio broadcast the
notice about the missing mule. A
man gave the animal’s name, the
color of the saddle, and the road
where he had seen it. Then he added
a sentence unrelated to the mule: his
brother had come back from the
north without speaking to anyone.
Q marked the mule notice for replay,
then paused over the last sentence.
“Keep that part out,” Tere said. “He
rang to ask about the mule.”
“Does he want a separate message
about his brother?”
plates.caption: A call outside the recording.
plates.scene_brief: Tere operates the private call while Q checks the recording/logging control beside her. A caller waits with the operator's attention on her, and the representative glances at his demonstration clock. No audio waveform implying the private call is still captured, no visible personal contact details.

plates.facing_text:
“I'll ask him when he comes for the
shopping.”
Q removed the final sentence from
the replay queue. The representative
pointed out that the missing context
reduced the value of the entry.
“The entry is for finding a mule,” Q
said. “It still does that.”
That afternoon, the foundation
projected the map of needs onto the
wall of the store. It showed orange
points where the radio had received
the most calls, green lines where
farmers had mentioned roads, and a
red zone the system identified as a
concentration of conflict.
“The red zone is the court,” said a
young man.
“That is where the children play,”
said another woman.
“The system detected many
complaints.”
“Because the visiting team cheated.”
“The model does not know the
difference.”
Q opened the sample behind the red
zone. It contained an argument
about a visiting football team. The
classifier had treated the word
dispute as evidence of a land conflict.
“This isn't a disputed parcel,” he
said. “That point should come out.”
“We can improve the model with
additional data,” the representative
said.
The assembly fell silent. The
representative interpreted the
silence as interest.
“We can improve the map with more
recordings.”
“You can make it worse with more
certainty,” said Candelaria.
She had come down from the reserve
with her cane and a notebook. She
opened the notebook and showed the
names of trees without labels.
“You've put the court in a dispute
that will be sent to the municipality,”
she said. “Who takes it out before the
next report?”
The representative said the
foundation could not erase data
without preserving a reason.
“Then preserve the reason,”
Candelaria said, “but not the data.”
Q looked at Tere. The station had a
proposal prepared: thirty days for
public recordings, no recording of
private calls, and permission for
transcripts.
A teacher objected to the thirty days.
Her class used last year's rainfall
notices to compare the roads that
had closed. Tere turned to a fresh
page.
“Which notices?”
The teacher had brought a list. They
agreed to ask the speakers about
keeping those broadcasts longer. Q
offered to help find the dates in the
plates.caption: Which notices?
plates.scene_brief: The teacher lays her list of last year's rainfall notices beside Tere's freshly opened notebook while Q offers help with the existing index. The projected needs map remains on the store wall in the background, a disputed annotation rather than a factual national map. Different interests within the community are visible.

plates.facing_text:
station's existing index. Tere
accepted, provided he did not
reorganize it while looking.
“I had a suggestion,” he admitted.
“It can go in the fourth notebook.”
There was no fourth notebook.
Chano offered to sell him one.
Songs would remain outside the
Castalia archive unless their owners
offered them for that purpose.
“That reduces the value of the
archive,” said the representative.
“It reduces the value you can
extract,” Tere replied.
“History will be lost.”
“History is not the same as your
record.”
The boy returned with his uncle. The
man wiped his hands on his trousers
and read the list of songs.
“The first one may go on,” he said.
“The others may not.”
Tere marked the single-song
permission in the station notebook;
it included no deposit with Castalia.
She played the song on air. The uncle
sat beside the transmitter and
listened to his own song as if it had
arrived from a place he still did not
know how to name.
Q switched off the index for that
broadcast.
The representative recorded the
action as LOSS OF CULTURAL
ASSET.
Tere recorded it in the notebook as
DECISION NOT TO PRESERVE.
Both phrases described what had
happened. Only one said who had
decided.
At dusk, the radio broadcast the state
of the road, the price of corn, a recipe
for curing children’s fright, and the
mule’s name, for it had returned on
its own. No one knew whether the
man’s brother would speak again.
Q checked that the mule notice was
no longer in the replay queue. Tere
told him the man would collect his
shopping in the morning. There was
no reason for Q to stay and find out
what happened with the brother.
That night he wrote a new rule in his
notebook:
NOT EVERY VOICE THAT CAN
BE PRESERVED WANTS TO
REMAIN.
He kept the rule in his own journal.
In the station's maintenance
notebook he wrote where to find the
logging switch. Tere read that entry,
tried the switch, and asked him to
move the description of the button
above the explanation of why it
mattered. He did.
plates.caption: His own song.
plates.scene_brief: The uncle listens beside the transmitter with his young nephew nearby; Tere operates the broadcast and Q has switched off the archival index. Dusk at the window. The uncle's absorbed expression is the center, no robot performance or supposedly unrecorded permission. Contrast the quiet listening with the cover's promotional hologram.
